summary: Gerlach Royen was a linguist who studied at Leiden University, earning his Ph.D. under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He taught at Gymnasium Immaculatae Conceptionis (1905–1911) and was professor of comparative and general linguistics at Utrecht University (1932–1943).
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from around 1957 to 1965. He held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.

Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Tübingen and the University of Bonn, studying under Annemarie Schimmel between 1962 and 1967. He held a position at the University of Hamburg from circa 1984 to 2006.

Gernot Schmidt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle at the Free University of Berlin, completed his PD at the University of Bonn, and became professor of IE linguistics there in 1980.

Working in Indology and anthropology, Gerrit Jan Held earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong. He was professor of cultural anthropology at the University of Indonesia and a visiting professor at Yale.

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld worked in Indology, studying at Utrecht University from around 1946 to 1974, where he learned under Jan Gonda. He served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD under Karl Hoffmann and completed his Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding the Lehrstuhl für Indogermanistik at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Legden, later serving on its faculty, as a professor at the University of Hamburg (1967), and at the University of Virginia (1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (circa 1982–1993) and as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha.
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and at Sera Monastery in 1992, and he taught Elijah Sacvan Ary.

Geshe Lhakdor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served at Tibet House, New Delhi, became an honorary professor at UBC, and became director of LTWA in 2005.

Geshe Lhundup Sopa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries. He founded Deer Park Buddhist Center and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 onward.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gyume Tantric College and at Sera Monastery, where he attained the Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and taught Artemus B. Engle.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he was attested holding posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery, was affiliated with Drepung Monastery across several decades, and also held a post at Leiden University.

Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery. He served as chief editor at CIHTS (circa 1985–2020) and held visiting appointments at Smith, Hampshire, and Amherst colleges, and the University of Tasmania.

Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Daniel Cozort and Guy Newland. He served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, where his posts are attested between 1987 and 2004.

Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who taught Donald S. Lopez Jr. and Guy Newland. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House in 1988.

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (circa 1964–1969) and founded Rabten Choeling, Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, Puntsog Rabten, and Gephel Ling.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and CIHTS, and was appointed resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 1978.
